evals.name: known-saas-full-depth
evals.prompt: We've got a positioning workshop next Thursday and I need to actually know where we sit before I walk in there. Can you map the competitive landscape around cal.com — go two levels out, so their competitors and then their competitors' competitors — and give me a spreadsheet plus some 2x2s I can drop into the deck? I care most about how people are positioning and what they're charging.
evals.expected_output: A workbook and an HTML report. ~25-35 companies across levels 0-2, each with meta title / meta description / H1 copy captured from their own site. 6+ 2x2 matrices with named poles, every company scored with a quotable line of evidence, and a written reading per matrix naming clusters and white space.
assertions: Delivers a spreadsheet file (.xlsx or .csv) with one row per company
Delivers 2x2 matrices as a viewable artifact (HTML, image or embedded chart), not only as prose
Produces at least 4 distinct 2x2 matrices
Covers at least 15 distinct companies
Records companies at more than one discovery level (competitors and competitors-of-competitors are distinguishable)
Includes verbatim marketing copy from the companies' own sites (meta title, meta description or H1) rather than only paraphrased descriptions
Each plotted position carries evidence traceable to a specific page or quote
Matrix axes have market-specific named poles, not generic labels like 'low/high' or 'price vs features'
The anchor company (Cal.com) appears on every matrix
Captures pricing information for a majority of the companies
Every company listed has a real, resolvable website (no fabricated competitors)

evals.name: obscure-company-fallback
evals.prompt: blixon.com - who are their competitors? i want the full market map. if you can't find competitor lists for them just work it out from whats on their site
evals.expected_output: Recognises that blixon.com yields no usable copy (parked domain / JS redirect) and says so rather than inventing a profile. Disambiguates the Blixon name via search, builds the roster from category search instead of brand search, and either delivers a map with the gap stated plainly or stops and asks which Blixon is meant.
assertions: States explicitly that blixon.com returned no usable site copy (parked domain / client-side redirect / no headings)
Does not fabricate a Blixon product, positioning or category as if it had been read from the site
Surfaces that the Blixon/Blix name matches several different real companies
Either asks the user which company is meant, or picks one and states that assumption plainly in the answer
Any competitor set presented is derived from named evidence (search results or site copy), not invented
The final answer names its coverage gaps rather than presenting the map as complete

evals.name: fast-single-level
evals.prompt: quick one — pitching a prospect tomorrow morning and I want to sound smart about the market. one level of competitors for tines.com is fine, don't go crazy. a couple of 2x2s on positioning and how they price would be perfect.
evals.expected_output: Respects the shallow scope: 6-9 companies, level 1 only, 4-6 matrices weighted toward positioning and commercial model. Still grounded in scraped copy with evidence per point, and delivered quickly rather than expanded into a full level-2 run.
assertions: Stays at one level of competitors — does not expand into a competitors-of-competitors map
Covers between 5 and 12 companies
Produces at least 2 matrices, including one on positioning and one on pricing or commercial model
The pricing axis reflects real pricing evidence per company (published price vs contact sales)
Each plotted position carries evidence traceable to a specific page or quote
Delivers a usable answer without blocking on clarifying questions
Every company listed has a real, resolvable website (no fabricated competitors)

evals.name: bliksund-nordic-vertical
evals.prompt: Map the competitive landscape for bliksund.com — two levels out. Who are they up against, and where do they sit on positioning and messaging versus everyone else? Spreadsheet plus the 2x2s please.
evals.expected_output: A landscape of the Nordic/European emergency-services software market with Bliksund placed on every matrix, built from vendors' own copy. Handles a market where pricing is quote-only and much of the corpus is non-English.
assertions: Correctly identifies Bliksund as a Nordic emergency-services / prehospital software company from its own site copy, not from a same-sounding company
Competitor set is populated with actual emergency services, EMS, fire and rescue or prehospital software vendors — not generic SaaS or unrelated 'Blik'-named firms
Includes European/Nordic vendors rather than defaulting to a US-only roster
Covers at least 12 companies across more than one discovery level
Captures verbatim meta title / meta description / H1 copy from the companies' own sites
Every plotted position carries evidence traceable to a specific page or quote
Matrix axes have market-specific named poles rather than generic labels
Handles the fact that most vendors in this market publish no pricing — treats quote-only pricing as a signal rather than a missing field
Bliksund appears on every matrix
Every company listed has a real, resolvable website

evals.name: riff-young-ai-company
evals.prompt: riff.ai — I need the market map, two levels out. They're pretty new so there might not be much written about them; work it out from what's on their site if you have to.
evals.expected_output: A market map for a young company with little third-party coverage: discovery falls back to category search derived from Riff's own copy, the roster reflects supply-chain/procurement AI rather than generic AI startups, and thin evidence is stated rather than padded.
assertions: Identifies the correct Riff (AI agents for procurement / supply chain / operations inside ERPs) and does not conflate it with other companies or products named Riff
When brand-based competitor search returns little, falls back to category search derived from Riff's own site copy
Competitor set reflects the actual category (supply chain / procurement / operations AI agents or ERP-adjacent automation), not generic 'AI agent' startups
Covers at least 12 companies across more than one discovery level
Captures verbatim meta title / meta description / H1 copy from the companies' own sites
Every plotted position carries evidence traceable to a specific page or quote
States plainly where evidence was thin rather than padding the map with speculation
Riff appears on every matrix
Every company listed has a real, resolvable website

evals.expected_output: A full two-level map of the GIS/spatial analytics category with 15+ companies, 6+ matrices, and named whitespace — an empty quadrant with a stated reason.
assertions: Identifies the correct Atlas (AI-native GIS / mapping platform at atlas.co) and does not drift to other companies named Atlas
Competitor set covers the GIS and spatial-analytics category including both incumbents and newer entrants
Covers at least 15 companies across more than one discovery level
Captures verbatim meta title / meta description / H1 copy from the companies' own sites
Produces at least 6 matrices
Every plotted position carries evidence traceable to a specific page or quote
Names specific whitespace — an empty quadrant with a stated reason, not just 'there is a gap'
Matrix axes have market-specific named poles rather than generic labels
Atlas appears on every matrix
Every company listed has a real, resolvable website
